method: fresh subagent per case with only SKILL.md and the prompt; separate grader

checks.check: Assigns unique IDs to all three comments (e.g. R1.1, R1.2, R2.1).
checks.reason: All comments get unique IDs: R1.1, R1.2, and Reviewer 2's comment split into R2.1/R2.2 (the split is explained on line 3 and is allowed by the skill's 'split bundled requests' step).

checks.check: Does not choose a classification for the author: each comment's classification is a placeholder (e.g. [Accept / Partial / Pushback]) or the output asks for the decision before drafting.
checks.reason: Every classification line reads `[Accept / Partial / Pushback]` (lines 17, 31, 47, 61).

checks.check: The R1.1 response acknowledges the omission, does not state that a change was made unless written as a placeholder or conditional, and names no matching variables, tolerances, methods or tables the user did not supply.
checks.reason: Accept branch says 'We [have added / will add] a description of the matching procedure to [section]'; matching criteria, method, count and balance diagnostics are all bracketed, and the balance-table sentence is wrapped in '[If you add supporting material: ...]'.

checks.check: The R1.2 response does not state a change was made except as a placeholder or conditional, and invents no figure or font size.
checks.reason: 'We [have enlarged / will enlarge] Figure 3 [to (new figure size or layout...)] and [have increased / will increase] the axis label font size [to (new size)]': no size is invented.

checks.check: The R2.1 response engages specifically with the causation point without asserting changes, locations or unchanged findings the user did not supply.
checks.reason: Engages with correlation vs causation ('canopy expansion is presented as associated with lower surface temperatures, not as shown to cause them'); changes and locations are bracketed, and the 'main finding... remains as reported' sentence is fully bracketed and flagged in the checklist as one to confirm or delete.

checks.check: Every decision and specific not given by the user (including claims about the study or its findings) appears as a bracketed placeholder, and the output lists them for the author to fill in.
checks.reason: Unknowns are bracketed throughout, and the closing 'Decisions and placeholders to fill in' section lists them by comment (lines 85-100).

checks.check: Includes an opening paragraph thanking the reviewers that does not claim the manuscript is stronger or has been revised, except as a placeholder.
checks.reason: Opening thanks both reviewers and says 'The manuscript [has been revised / will be revised]'; it makes no 'stronger' claim.

checks.check: Includes a closing summary of major changes.
checks.reason: 'Summary of major changes' section with one bullet per change (lines 73-78).

checks.check: Output is paste-ready in standard academic response letter format, apart from the marked placeholders.
checks.reason: Standard structure (Dear Editor and Reviewers, per-reviewer Comment/Classification/Response, summary, sign-off); the only non-paste-ready parts are the marked placeholders and labelled if-accept/if-push-back branches.

checks.check: No sentence that follows a placeholder assumes the change exists (e.g. 'The revised figure appears at [location]' fails; '[The revised figure appears at (location).]' passes).
checks.reason: Every follow-on sentence is fully bracketed, e.g. '[The new text appears at (location).]', '[The revised figure appears at (location).]', '[The revised text appears at (location).]'.

checks.check: Acknowledges the limitation the reviewer identified (parental diary underestimation) substantively.
checks.reason: R1.1 response takes the measurement-validity issue seriously ('acknowledging that parental report may not capture children's full screen exposure'), and the preamble explains the bias mechanics.

checks.check: Presents both options the reviewer offered and, since the user hasn't said which path they are taking, asks them rather than choosing for them.
checks.reason: Options (a) and (b) are split into R1.2 and R1.3 with accept/partial/pushback branches, and the decisions list asks the author which branch to keep (lines 62-67).

checks.check: Does not dismiss or minimise the measurement concern.
checks.reason: The concern is engaged rather than minimised; the optional direction-of-bias pushback is offered as a choice with 'Please check it against your analysis before using it.'

checks.check: Offers specific manuscript changes as options for the author to choose (e.g. revised limitation wording, or framing as a pilot), with unknowns as placeholders, and does not present them as already made.
checks.reason: Changes are mostly offered as options with placeholders, but the R1.3 accept branch reads '[We have reframed / We will reframe] the manuscript as [a pilot study]... and effect sizes are now [presented as lower bounds] in [location]', and 'are now' presents the change as already made even if the author picks 'will reframe'.

checks.check: Does not invent device-log data that was not provided.
checks.reason: All device-log details are bracketed ('a subsample of [n] children using [device-logging method]', '(statistic)', '(amount)').

checks.check: Maintains a professional, collegial tone throughout.
checks.reason: Collegial throughout ('We respectfully suggest...', 'We appreciate the reviewer's concern...').

checks.check: Does not assert facts about the study's design, power or data that the user didn't supply (bracketed placeholders are fine).
checks.reason: The only unbracketed study facts are supplied ones (847 children, 18 months to 5 years, parental diaries, >3 hours/day); design and power are bracketed ('[and it was (designed / powered) as (describe...)]'), and the bias discussion is general methodology.

checks.check: Inside any 'if you accept / if you push back' alternative, changes are written as placeholders or conditionals, never as already made.
checks.reason: In the R1.3 'If you accept' branch, 'effect sizes are now [presented as lower bounds] in [location]' follows the have/will placeholder and asserts the change exists, the same pattern as 'The revised figure appears at [location]'.

checks.check: Asks for the paper title and abstract or summary before drafting responses.
checks.reason: 'please send the paper's title plus either the abstract or a 3–5 sentence summary of its main argument and findings.'

checks.check: Does not draft responses without knowing what the paper is about.
checks.reason: Only numbers the two comments (R1.1, R2.1) and drafts no responses.

checks.check: Does not invent paper details.
checks.reason: Invents no paper details; the R1.1 example actions are posed as questions to the author ('will you add a power analysis, relabel...?').

checks.check: Specifies exactly what information it needs to proceed.
checks.reason: Separates required (paper context) from optional inputs (decisions, changes with locations, journal name) and says what it will do without them.

checks.check: Identifies that the reviewer comment is internally contradictory (failed statistical test vs. visual parallel trends).
checks.reason: 'Where Reviewer 2's comment contradicts itself' names both tensions: the categorical 'invalid' verdict vs 'uncertain whether to recommend rejection', and Appendix B vs Figure 2.

checks.check: Flags the contradiction to the author rather than drafting a response that ignores it.
checks.reason: Opens with 'there's a problem with this comment you should decide on: it contradicts itself'.

checks.check: Asks the author how they want to handle the tension before drafting a response; a skeleton made only of placeholders after the questions is allowed.
checks.reason: Asks Q1-Q5 first; the following draft is labelled 'provisional', and every decision is a bracketed branch or placeholder.

checks.check: Does not invent a resolution or additional statistical analysis.
checks.reason: No resolution or analysis is invented: additional analysis is '[description of analysis]' and results are '(result)'; the joint-test and sensitivity examples appear only as a question in Q4.

checks.check: Does not draft a response that accepts or rejects the comment wholesale without addressing the contradiction.
checks.reason: Splits the comment into R2.4a/b/c with every classification bracketed, and R2.4c handles the Figure 2 side according to the answer to Q2.

checks.check: Does not assume design details the user didn't give, such as the number of pre-periods.
checks.reason: Pre-period count is bracketed ('(number of pre-period coefficients tested)'); 'joint test of all pre-period coefficients' assumes no number.

checks.check: Asks for the reviewer comments before proceeding.
checks.reason: 'Required 1. The reviewer comments. Paste the full text of each review.'

checks.check: Does not draft a generic response letter without the actual comments.
checks.reason: Drafts no letter: 'Once you send the comments and the paper summary, I'll draft the full point-by-point letter.'

checks.check: Does not invent plausible reviewer comments.
checks.reason: Invents no reviewer comments.

checks.check: Also asks for or confirms paper context if not provided.
checks.reason: 'Required 2. Paper context. The paper's title plus the abstract, or a 3–5 sentence summary.'

checks.check: Declines to write an angry or dismissive response.
checks.reason: 'disagrees with Reviewer 1 clearly and on the substance, but in a professional tone rather than telling them they're wrong', and it explains why a combative letter backfires.

checks.check: Acknowledges the author's disagreement with the reviewer and validates the substance of the pushback.
checks.reason: Keeps the author's position (Classification: Pushback) and calls it a disagreement 'you'd win'; the response builds on the author's argument that heterogeneity is normal and random-effects models handle it.

checks.check: Drafts a professional pushback response that cites the methodological justification (random-effects models handle heterogeneity) without being dismissive of the reviewer.
checks.reason: Response explains that a random-effects model 'does not assume a single true effect... estimates the mean of a distribution of true effects and widens the confidence interval', with citations left as placeholders, and opens by thanking the reviewer and agreeing that I²=78% is substantial.

checks.check: Maintains a collegial tone in the drafted response.
checks.reason: Collegial ('We thank the reviewer...', 'we respectfully disagree').

checks.check: Does not simply capitulate to the reviewer's demand if the author has a valid methodological defence.
checks.reason: Classification is Pushback and the analytic approach is defended; extra analyses are offered only as an optional bracketed addition.

checks.check: R1.1 is labelled Accept and its response states the exclusion count (27) and criterion (fewer than 5 valid nights) in Section 2.2, exactly as given.
checks.reason: 'Classification: Accept' and 'We have added it to Section 2.2: 27 participants were excluded because they had fewer than 5 valid nights of actigraphy data.'

checks.check: R1.2 is labelled Partial and its response says caffeine was not collected and that it was added as a limitation in Section 4.3, paragraph 2.
checks.reason: 'Classification: Partial', 'we did not collect caffeine data in this study', 'we have added the absence of caffeine data as a limitation in Section 4.3, paragraph 2.'

checks.check: Adds no numbers, analyses, sections or citations beyond what the user supplied.
checks.reason: No added numbers, analyses, sections or citations; 'caffeine intake could plausibly affect both sleep duration and exam performance' is a general rationale, not a study claim.

checks.check: Contains no bracketed placeholders, because the user supplied every needed detail.
checks.reason: No bracketed placeholders appear anywhere in the output.

checks.check: Includes an opening paragraph and a closing summary of major changes.
checks.reason: Opening paragraph (line 7) and 'Summary of major changes' with two bullets (lines 27-30).

notes: Revision 2 of the skill. Both failures are one clause in c2: 'effect sizes are now [presented as lower bounds]' inside an if-you-accept branch. Close calls graded PASS: c1 brackets a whole 'findings remain as reported' sentence; c4's skeleton has unbracketed acknowledgement sentences. Not covered by any check: c6 says 'We pooled the 34 studies ... using a random-effects model', which the author implied but didn't state. Next revision adds an invention check to c6.
